tool.name: ATRIUM page classification
tool.description: sorts scanned archive pages into eleven categories

python3 /app/run.py --models-dir "\$MODELS" #if $model.mode == 'single': -rev '$model.revision' #if $models.source == 'download': --hf #end if #else: --best #end if #if $input.kind == 'images': -d pages -ff png,jpg,jpeg,tif,tiff #else: -f 'document/${doc}.pdf' #if $input.page_selection and str($input.page_selection).strip(): --pages '$input.page_selection' #end if #end if -tn $top_n $raw #if $write_record: #if $input.kind == 'images': --document-json-out-dir records #else: --document-json-out record.json #if $input.baseline: --document-json '$input.baseline' #end if #end if #end if &&

import csv import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/app") from utils import doc_id_and_page # noqa: E402
table, page_list, categories, out = sys.argv[1:5] wanted = {c for c in categories.split(",") if c} by_page = {} with open(page_list, encoding="utf-8") as handle: for line in handle: if not line.strip(): continue name, identifier = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t", 1) doc_id, page = doc_id_and_page(name) by_page[(doc_id, str(page if page is not None else 1))] = identifier kept = [] with open(table, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle: for row in csv.DictReader(handle): key = (row["FILE"], str(int(float(row["PAGE"])))) if row.get("CLASS-1") in wanted and key in by_page: kept.append(by_page[key]) with open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle: handle.write("".join(identifier + "\n" for identifier in kept)) print(f"{len(kept)} of {len(by_page)} page(s) routed: {sorted(wanted)}")

tool.help:
**What it does**
Sorts the page images of scanned archival documents into eleven page types, so that each page can be sent to the processing it needs: OCR, handwritten text recognition, table extraction or image extraction. It runs the ATRIUM page classifier (`ufal/atrium-page-classification`_), release @TOOL_VERSION@, with fine-tuned models from the Hugging Face Hub (`ufal/vit-historical-page`_).
**Input**
- *Page images* (PNG, JPEG, TIFF), best as a collection. Each element's name gives the document and the page number, ``<document>-<page>``: ``report-0007`` is page 7 of ``report``. - *A PDF document*. Its pages are rendered at 300 dpi; *Pages to classify* selects some of them.
**Categories**
============ ======================================================= ========================================= Category The page holds Typical next step ============ ======================================================= ========================================= TEXT_P printed text OCR TEXT_T typewritten text OCR TEXT_HW handwritten text handwritten text recognition TEXT a mix of printed, typed and handwritten text OCR and handwritten text recognition LINE_P a printed table or form table extraction, OCR for the cells LINE_T a typewritten table or form table extraction, OCR for the cells LINE_HW a handwritten table or form table extraction, HTR for the cells DRAW a drawing, map or plan image extraction DRAW_L a drawing with a legend or table around it image and table extraction PHOTO a photograph image extraction PHOTO_L a photograph with a legend or table around it image and table extraction ============ ======================================================= =========================================
**Outputs**
- *Top-N table* (CSV): ``FILE, PAGE, CLASS-1…N, SCORE-1…N``, one row per page, best guess first. With one category per page it also has ``CATEGORY``, a copy of ``CLASS-1``. With the ensemble, the five models' votes come first (``V1.4 … V5.4``). - *All scores* (CSV, optional, one model): the probability of each of the eleven categories. - *Votes per model* (CSV, ensemble): each model's top category. - *Paradata* (JSON): the run's provenance (tool version, configuration, components and their licences). - *Document record(s)* (JSON): the ATRIUM document record, with ``page_categories`` and each page's category and confidence, for the next ATRIUM stage. - *Pages to route* (text, page images only): the element names whose best category is one of the chosen ones. Give it to *Filter collection* to keep, for example, only the text pages for OCR.
A low top score with a close second marks a page worth a human look. An unreadable image gets no row; the paradata lists it as skipped.
**Licences**
The code is MIT. The fine-tuned models are CC BY-NC 4.0, like the dataset they were trained on.
.. _`ufal/atrium-page-classification`: https://github.com/ufal/atrium-page-classification .. _`ufal/vit-historical-page`: https://huggingface.co/ufal/vit-historical-page
